scope: Little-toe / continuous forefoot attachment repair; preserved existing hand geometry
method: Original parametric foot and toe volumes are fused into one closed skin mesh; smooth field unions create metatarsal webs and a broad plantar support. Semantic regions share vertices and smooth normals. Cached immutable rest topology supplies independent pose buffers. The root-to-contact blend and its deformation Jacobian carry skin normals and projected nail/crease lines through the five-second heel rise.
repairs: Removed disconnected lateral toe and exposed proximal tube cap.
Replaced overlapping toe/forefoot shells with continuous manifold geometry.
Kept the little toe short and distinct while joining its plantar and dorsal base to the metatarsals.
Matched the leg-edition ankle contour and normals to the existing shin loft.
Computed per-region bounds from indexed vertices for local focus and picking.
Preserved the five-second action, exact endpoints and independent mirrored body instances.

visualReview.renderer: Chrome WebGL / Three.js 0.186.1; actual imported source models under FORM-style lighting
visualReview.views: Foot: front, lateral, medial, quarter and underside at 0 and 2.5 seconds; fifth toe selected at both poses. Leg: whole form and close ankle/foot at both poses. Full body: mirrored feet close at both poses. Existing hand: front, lateral and back at both poses.
observations: Little toe joins the lateral forefoot without a gap or separate cap at rest and rise.
Five toes remain legible in front, side and underside views; the broad forefoot supports their roots.
Toe nail margins remain attached to the skin, with restrained joint creases.
No holes appear at leg/foot or mirrored full-body attachments.
Existing hand pinky is continuous into the palm at rest and full grasp; hand source was left unchanged.
visualReview.playback: Executed an actual 5.15-second requestAnimationFrame foot loop (159 rendered frames); visual judgment used the rendered rest/peak/multiview samples, rather than claiming continuous human review.

notes: Procedural illustrative surface anatomy; no external scan/model assets. No SVG changes or MP4 output.
